fixer.summary: T-121 is fixed. A surplus Heroic Inspiration now goes only to a living player character who lacks it. Before, `grant_heroic_inspiration` (dungdra/rest.py) gave it to whatever creature the `give_inspiration` answer named, monsters included. Now the answer has to match one of the PCs who lack it. Any other name, like a monster or a PC who already has it, gives it to no one: the engine logs that it can't give it there (R-50), and then that the new instance is lost (R-51). The give/lost log events now cite page 183 and `GLOSS.heroic-inspiration#3`; before, they cited page 8 and had no clause. The same check also makes T-122's test (`test_heroic_inspiration_cant_be_given_to_a_pc_who_has_it`) pass. With --runxfail, the T-121 and T-122 tests pass, the unit suite passes (575 tests), ruff check and ruff format are clean, and dev-gate passes. One related test still fails with --runxfail: `test_heroic_inspiration_a_monster_cant_gain_it`. It belongs to T-120 (granting Heroic Inspiration directly to a monster), which is disputed and wasn't part of this ticket.

followups.title: Game.decide returns a pre-set or decider answer without checking it against the offered options (dungdra/game.py:82), so any caller that resolves the answer with game.get(pick) can act on a creature the rule never offered. Validate answers against `options` in decide (refuse or fall back to default) so each rule doesn't need its own guard like grant_heroic_inspiration now has.

review.summary:
I'm approving this fix. Before it, grant_heroic_inspiration looked up whatever creature the answer named with game.get(pick), and that's how a monster could end up with Heroic Inspiration. Now it only matches the answer against `lacking`, the list of living player characters who don't have Heroic Inspiration. That list was already the place the rule was decided, so the fix uses the existing mechanism instead of adding a second one. If the answer names anyone else, the engine logs a refusal citing R-50 and then logs the usual "lost" event. Both R-50 and R-51 say exactly this. The citations on the surplus logs are corrected to page=183 and rule=GLOSS.heroic-inspiration#3.

The same guard also fixes T-122, a gift to a player character who already has Heroic Inspiration, so both strict xfails come off. That's acceptable scope, since one guard enforces both halves of clause #3. I didn't run the tests myself; the gates report all passing.

The new unit tests check real outcomes: the return value, each creature's heroic_inspiration flag, and the logged rule. None of them just reads the code's own constants back.

There's no special-casing for test fixtures or particular monsters. One small leftover I didn't count against the fix: the code path for a first-time gain still cites page 8 with no clause number, but the diff doesn't touch it.

I've filed one follow-up. game.decide doesn't check an answer against the options it offered, so other callers can be tricked the same way.
